seo.title: Security Checklist for Web3 Frontend Developers
seo.description: A comprehensive checklist covering wallet integration, transaction security, and dApp security best practices for Web3 frontend development.

content.intro: Frontend security in Web3 protects users from phishing, transaction manipulation, and data theft. Use this checklist to secure your dApp.

items.text: Never request more permissions than needed from wallets
Handle wallet disconnection gracefully without crashes
Validate wallet address format before using
Support multiple wallets, not just MetaMask
Detect and handle network/chain switching
Show clear UI states for connecting, connected, and disconnected
Persist connection state appropriately (don't reconnect without consent)
Handle wallet extension conflicts gracefully
Always simulate transactions before sending to catch errors
Show clear transaction details before user signs
Display gas estimates in both native token and USD
Implement transaction status tracking (pending/confirmed/failed)
Handle transaction reverts with user-friendly error messages
Validate all user inputs before including in transactions
Check token allowances before attempting transfers
Warn users about unlimited token approvals
Implement transaction timeout handling
Provide speedup/cancel options for stuck transactions
Use typed data signing (EIP-712) instead of raw message signing
Display human-readable message content before signing
Include domain separator in typed data to prevent replay attacks
Add nonces to signatures to prevent reuse
Include expiry timestamps in time-sensitive signatures
Never sign messages containing raw transaction data
Validate signature requests come from your own frontend
Sanitize all URL parameters before use
Validate address inputs match expected format (checksummed)
Validate amount inputs are positive numbers
Check for integer overflow in amount calculations
Validate token decimals match expected values
Sanitize ENS names before resolution
Validate contract addresses exist and have code
Escape special characters in user-provided data
Never store private keys in frontend code or storage
Do not store sensitive data in localStorage
Clear sensitive data from memory after use
Use HTTPS for all API calls
Validate SSL certificates for RPC endpoints
Do not log sensitive transaction data
Implement proper error handling to avoid leaking stack traces
Verify contract addresses against known good addresses
Display clear warnings for unknown contracts
Show full destination addresses, not just truncated versions, for large transactions
Implement address book for frequent recipients
Warn about address poisoning attacks
Display ENS verification alongside addresses
Check token contracts against known scam lists
Implement error boundaries to prevent full app crashes
Handle RPC errors gracefully with retry logic
Display user-friendly error messages, not raw errors
Log errors for debugging without exposing sensitive data
Handle network timeouts with appropriate fallbacks
Implement circuit breakers for failing services
Audit npm packages for known vulnerabilities (npm audit)
Lock dependency versions to prevent supply chain attacks
Use integrity hashes for CDN resources
Review dependency code for wallet or key handling
Implement Content Security Policy headers
Avoid using eval() or innerHTML with user data
Minify and obfuscate production builds
Test with real wallets on testnets, not just mocks
Test mobile wallet browser behavior
Test with slow network conditions
Test transaction failures and reverts
Test wallet disconnection mid-transaction
Test with multiple browser extensions installed
Implement E2E tests with wallet automation (Synpress)
